title.purpose: Semibold panel names and emphasized telemetry labels.

body.purpose: Process rows, controls, and ordinary values; user-adjustable from 10 to 16 px.

measurement.purpose: Prominent live values and application title moments.

label.purpose: Table headings, summaries, status, and legends.

micro.purpose: Graph axes and dense meter annotations only.

motion.name: telemetry-window
motion.purpose: Bounds retained graph data by elapsed time and by the hard capacity required for the 250 ms minimum polling interval.

motion.name: chart-interpolation-delay
motion.purpose: Allows smooth movement using only real samples.

motion.name: chart-frame-rate
motion.purpose: User-selectable redraw cadence for live graphs; 30 fps is the default.

dataSeries.mapping: Zero-based logical-core index. Reuse cyclically only when the machine reports more than 24 logical cores.

temperature.interpolation: continuous RGB interpolation between adjacent stops; clamp outside the endpoints

cpuLegend.item: 10px swatch, CPU number, flexible spacer, right-aligned percentage

networkScale.labelFormat: format each scale × fraction as a network rate
networkScale.contract: Plot and right-side labels use the same computed maximum from the bounded retained history.

gpuTelemetryLayout.meters: Two side-by-side 320px blocks with 8px tracks, 36px labels, and 112px right-aligned values.
gpuTelemetryLayout.migration: GpuDetails is a legacy deserialization variant only; normalization removes its tile and the main GPU panel owns all details.

curve.lines: anti-aliased cubic Bézier strokes with control points clamped to each sampled interval
curve.interpolation: Catmull-Rom clamped to the endpoints of each sampled interval

geometry.cpuSubdivision: one quad emitted as two triangles

allocation.cpuPrimer: one transparent bounded batch completes the final CPU triangle count from the first usable frame
allocation.gpuGaps: missing device, utilization, or memory samples split the line and never bridge the missing interval

windowBackground.reason: The complete rendered root is opaque.

measuredEvidence.baselineRelease: 147 MiB to 417 MiB by 45 seconds; 57% average CPU
measuredEvidence.optimizedRelease: 153 MiB and stable for 70 seconds; 31% average CPU

components.name: Ruled Telemetry Graph
components.description: The low-cost GPU-rendered frame: lines use anti-aliased clamped Bézier strokes, the CPU stack uses bounded four-step Catmull-Rom triangles, and missing GPU samples are never bridged.
components.css: .ds-chart { margin: 0; color: #6f6b72; font: 400 10px 'Noto Sans', Ubuntu, sans-serif; } .ds-chart-row { display: flex; gap: 8px; } .ds-chart-frame { flex: 1; height: 90px; border: 1px solid #d9d9d9; background-color: #fff; background-image: linear-gradient(to right, rgba(216,218,221,.69) 1px, transparent 1px), linear-gradient(to bottom, #d8dadd 1px, transparent 1px); background-size: 16.666% 100%, 100% 20%; overflow: hidden; } .ds-chart svg { width: 100%; height: 100%; fill: none; stroke-width: 1.8; } .ds-chart .ds-rx { stroke: #3584e4; } .ds-chart .ds-tx { stroke: #ff7800; } .ds-chart-scale { width: 64px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; justify-content: space-between; text-align: right; font-size: 9px; } .ds-chart-axis { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; padding-right: 72px; margin-top: 4px; } .ds-network-footer { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 8px; padding-top: 8px; margin-top: 8px; border-top: 1px solid #d9d9d9; } .ds-network-footer > div { flex: 1; min-width: 180px; padding: 0 8px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 4px; } .ds-network-footer > div:not(:last-child) { border-right: 1px solid #d9d9d9; } .ds-network-footer b { color: #3d3846; font-weight: 600; } .ds-network-footer span { display: flex; gap: 12px; } .ds-network-footer i { color: #1c71d8; font-style: normal; } .ds-network-footer em { color: #c64600; font-style: normal; } .ds-network-footer small { color: #6f6b72; } .ds-core-legend { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 1fr); gap: 4px 20px; margin-top: 8px; } .ds-core-legend span { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; } .ds-core-legend i { width: 10px; height: 10px; background: #e01b24; } .ds-core-legend b { flex: 1; text-align: right; color: #3d3846; font-weight: 400; } .ds-chart:focus-within { outline: 2px solid #3584e4; outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.overview:
Strata should feel immediately at home on a contemporary Ubuntu desktop: pale neutral workspace, crisp white instruments, Noto Sans, compact controls, and quiet gray rules. The interface is an operating surface for sustained observation, so density, legibility, and stable visual meaning carry more weight than decoration.

Panels expose their configurability without turning the workspace into an editor. A small grip, a plain width control, a recoverable hide action, and a restrained resize edge remain visible as part of the instrument. Color is reserved for live series, measurements, selection, sorting, and active state.

Motion belongs to measured time. Graphs may move as samples advance; the rest of the interface remains still. Smooth curves stay within the values of adjacent samples, histories remain bounded, and missing telemetry is stated rather than visually fabricated.
keyCharacteristics: Pale neutral workspace with white, thinly ruled panels.
Compact GNOME-like controls and dense, readable data rows.
Blue active and sort states; categorical color identifies telemetry.
Visible but restrained grip, hide, span, and resize affordances.
Integrated GPU identity, metrics, meters, and history in one ordered instrument.
Real-time graph movement with bounded data and no decorative animation.

rules.name: The Signal Color Rule
rules.body: Use color to identify a series, value, selection, sort, or active state; do not spend it on empty decoration.

rules.name: The Honest Absence Rule
rules.body: Render unavailable numeric measurements as an em dash and unavailable subsystems with explicit text such as “Not configured” or the reported error.

rules.name: The Native Voice Rule
rules.body: Keep labels in sentence case and use standard uppercase only for established technical terms such as CPU, GPU, RAM, VRAM, PID, TCP, and UDP.

rules.name: The Ruled Surface Rule
rules.body: Use tone, separators, and spacing to establish depth; do not add cards inside panels, drop shadows, blur, or translucency.

dos: Do preserve the pale GNOME-like density, Noto Sans hierarchy, white panels, and thin gray separators.
Do keep panel grip, width, hide, and resize affordances visible, restrained, and recoverable.
Do preserve the full 24-core legend and its stable correspondence to the CPU graph layers.
Do keep the CPU legend column-major and dynamically limited to one through four equal columns.
Do derive network plot geometry and its right-side labels from one exact rounded scale.
Do keep GPU detail metrics integrated in the main GPU panel and normalize legacy standalone detail tiles away.
Do use the shared continuous five-stop temperature scale for CPU and GPU temperatures.
Do right-align numeric table data, left-align commands and users, and expose active sorting in blue with an arrow.
Do show unavailable values explicitly with an em dash or specific status copy.
Do keep graph histories bounded to both 62 seconds and 249 samples, and keep smooth interpolation within adjacent sampled values.
Do preserve direct CPU triangle emission and the transparent CPU allocation primer.
donts: Don't add decorative motion; real-time graph movement is the system's only continuous animation.
Don't add shadows, glass effects, nested decorative cards, oversized type, or spacious marketing-page rhythms.
Don't hide or simplify away the panel configurability that distinguishes Strata.
Don't restore a standalone GPU details panel or split its NVTOP-derived reading order across panels.
Don't replace direct CPU triangle emission with a chart library or per-frame polygon tessellation.
Don't bridge missing GPU samples or remove the CPU primer that stabilizes the final upload allocation.
Don't fabricate zeroes for missing telemetry or let interpolation imply measurements that were never sampled.
